questions.question: 5 boys P, Q, R, S and T are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). T is second to the left of P. R is second to the left of Q. R is third to the left of S. Who is sitting at the right end of the row?
questions.solution:
Logic followed here is the step-by-step arrangement of **5 boys** (P, Q, R, S, and T) facing **North**.

1. T is second to the left of P.

2. R is second to the left of Q.

3. R is third to the left of S.

**Final Arrangement:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/14ae2c187402b46b47c0612b0675276339f52d8ae93f13712d9a0678208261da.png] 

The person sitting at the **right end** of the row is **S**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

questions.question: A certain number of persons are standing in a row facing south. Q is standing second from the right end of the row. S is standing seventh to the left of M. Only one person stand between S and O, when counted towards right of S. Only two persons stand between Q and M. O is fourth to the right of R. Who among the following person stands eight to the right of O?
questions.solution:
According to the given information, a certain number of persons are facing **south** in a row. In a south-facing arrangement, the **right** direction is towards our left and the **left** direction is towards our right.

**Step-by-step derivation:**

**1) Q is standing second from the right end of the row:**

If we number the positions starting from the **right end** as 1, then **Q** is at position 2.

**2) Only two persons stand between Q and M:**

Since **Q** is at position 2, there are two positions (3 and 4) between them, making **M** at position 5.

**3) S is standing seventh to the left of M:**

Facing south, the left direction moves towards higher position numbers. So, **S** is at position 5 + 7 = 12.

**4) Only one person stands between S and O, when counted towards the right of S:**

The right direction moves towards lower position numbers. One person between position 12 (S) and **O** means **O** is at position 10 (with position 11 being the person between them).

**5) O is fourth to the right of R:**

If **O** is to the right of **R**, then **R** must be to the left of **O** (higher number position). **R** is at position 10 + 4 = 14.

**The arrangement can be summarized in the following table:**

Now, we need to find who stands **eighth to the right of O**:

Position of **O** = 10

Counting 8 positions towards the right (lower numbers): 10 − 8 = 2

At position 2, the person standing is **Q**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

questions.question: A certain number of persons are standing in a row facing south. B is standing at the right end of the row. C is standing sixth to the left of N. Only two persons stand between C and P, when counted towards right of C. Only three persons stand between B and N. C is second to the right of L. Who among the following person stands fifth to the right of L?
questions.solution:
Based on the given information, we can determine the arrangement of persons in the row. Since the persons are facing **South**, their **Left** and **Right** directions will be as follows:

 
• **Right** direction: Towards the **Left** side of the viewer.
 
• **Left** direction: Towards the **Right** side of the viewer.

**Step-by-step Arrangement:**

1. **B** is standing at the **right end** of the row.

2. Only **three persons** stand between **B** and **N**.

Position: (Right end) **B** > _ > _ > _ > **N**

3. **C** is standing **sixth to the left** of **N** (towards the viewer's right).

Position: **B** (1) > _ (2) > _ (3) > _ (4) > **N** (5) > _ (6) > _ (7) > _ (8) > _ (9) > _ (10) > **C** (11)

4. **C** is **second to the right** of **L** (This means **L** is at position 13, so that **C** at 11 is 2nd to its right).

Position: **B** (1) ... **N** (5) ... **C** (11) > _ (12) > **L** (13)

5. Only **two persons** stand between **C** and **P**, when counted towards the **right** of **C**.

Counting from **C** (11) towards the right (towards 1): positions 10 and 9 are between them, so **P** is at position 8.

Therefore, **P** stands fifth to the right of **L**.

questions.question: A bag contains 20 apples. If 4 apples are rotten, what percentage are good?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total apples = 20

Rotten apples = 4

**Calculation:**

Good apples = 20 − 4 = 16

Percentage of good apples = (16 / 20) × 100

= 80%

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 2".**

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and sixth number is related to fifth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 - Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

8548 : 8586 :: 1104 : ? :: 5435 : 5473
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic: Second Number = First Number + 38**

For the first pair **8548 : 8586**

⇒ 8548 + 38 = 8586

Applying the same logic to the third pair **5435 : 5473**

⇒ 5435 + 38 = 5473

Now, applying the same logic to the second pair to find the missing number

**1104 : ?**

⇒ 1104 + 38 = 1142

Hence, the correct answer is **'Option 3'**.

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 10 AM and 11 AM will the angle between the hour and the minute hand of a clock be 165 degrees?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The **hour hand** covers 360° in 12 hours.

Angular distance covered by the **hour hand** in 1 hour = 360 / 12 = 30°

Angular distance covered by the **hour hand** in 1 minute = 30 / 60 = 0.5°

The **minute hand** covers 360° in 60 minutes.

Angular distance covered by the **minute hand** in 1 minute = 360 / 60 = 6°

__Calculation:__

The given time is between **10 AM** and **11 AM**. Let the time be **10:M**.

Position of the **hour hand** at 10:M (taking 12:00 as 0°):

Angle = (10 × 30°) + (M × 0.5°) = 300° + 0.5M

Position of the **minute hand** at 10:M:

Angle = M × 6° = 6M

The absolute difference between these angles is given as **165 degrees**:

| (300 + 0.5M) − 6M | = 165

| 300 − 5.5M | = 165

**Case 1:**

300 − 5.5M = 165

5.5M = 300 − 165

5.5M = 135

M = 135 / 5.5 = 270 / 11

M ≈ 24.545

Rounding to the nearest whole number, M ≈ **25 minutes**.

**Case 2:**

300 − 5.5M = −165

5.5M = 300 + 165

5.5M = 465

M = 465 / 5.5 ≈ 84.54 (This exceeds 60 minutes, so it falls outside the 10 AM to 11 AM range).

Therefore, the time is approximately **10:25 AM**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle θ between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** is given by:

θ = |30H - {11 over 2}M|

Here, H = 10 and θ = 165°.

165 = |30 × 10 − 5.5M|

165 = |300 − 5.5M|

135 = 5.5M

M = 135 / 5.5 ≈ 24.54

Hence, the approximate time is **10:25 AM**.

The correct answer is **10:25**.

questions.question: A watch is 5 minutes slow at 12 AM. It gains 10 seconds every hour. When will it show the correct time (in AM) again?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The watch is **5 minutes slow** at 12:00 AM.

It gains **10 seconds every hour**.

**Calculation:**

Initial loss = 5 minutes = 300 seconds

Gain per hour = 10 seconds

Time required to recover 300 seconds = 300 ÷ 10 = 30 hours

30 hours after 12:00 AM = 6:00 AM (next day)

Since the question asks **in AM**, the watch will show the correct time again at **6:00 AM**.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 3".**
